record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Determine conditions under which the Petrie path of a chiral polytope is a polygon.

evidence.quote: Problem 8 Determine conditions under which the Petrie path of a chiral polytope is a polygon.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope of rank $n$ is a partially ordered set $\mathcal{P}$ of "faces" (with a minimum face $F_{-1}$ and maximum face $F_n$) satisfying the standard diamond and flag-connectedness conditions of Schulte–McMullen, so that maximal chains (flags) all have length $n+1$ and any two flags differing only in their rank-$i$ face are well defined for each $i\in\{0,\dots,n-1\}$. The polytope is called chiral if its automorphism group has exactly two orbits on flags, with adjacent flags lying in different orbits, so that $\mathcal{P}$ admits all combinatorial rotations but no combinatorial reflection.

For a chiral polytope $\mathcal{P}$ of rank $n$ with distinguished base flag $\Phi$ and standard rotation generators $\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}$ of its rotation group $\Gamma^+(\mathcal{P})$ (where $\sigma_i$ fixes all faces of $\Phi$ outside ranks $i-1,i$ and cyclically rotates within those ranks), define the Petrie element
$$\pi := \sigma_1\sigma_2\cdots\sigma_{n-1}.$$
The Petrie path of $\mathcal{P}$ (starting from $\Phi$) is the sequence of vertices traced by the iterates of $\pi$ acting on $\Phi$; equivalently, it is the orbit structure produced by repeatedly applying $\pi$, generalizing the notion of a Petrie polygon of a regular polytope.

Problem. Find necessary and sufficient combinatorial or group-theoretic conditions on a chiral abstract polytope $\mathcal{P}$ under which its Petrie path closes up into a (finite, non-self-intersecting) polygon.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search surfaces general literature on Petrie polygons, Petrie schemes, and chiral polytopes (including left/right Petrie polygons for chiral 4-polytopes), but does not produce a paper that explicitly settles the question of giving necessary and sufficient conditions for the Petrie path of a chiral polytope to be a polygon. The problem appears to remain unresolved in the surveyed literature.

status_evidence.title: Petrie Schemes (Gordon Williams)
status_evidence.snippet: Petrie schemes generalize Petrie polygons in abstract polytopes; results are known for regular cases but not stated for chiral polytopes.
status_evidence.claim: General theory of Petrie schemes addresses regular polytopes, leaving chiral cases as open territory.

status_evidence.title: Symmetry of Polytopes and Polyhedra (Schulte)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of regular and chiral abstract polytopes; lists structural problems regarding chiral polytopes.
status_evidence.claim: Standard survey discusses chiral polytopes without resolving the Petrie-path-as-polygon question.
